newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's TMA cargo carrier boosts capital.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's TMA cargo carrier boosts capital.

text.p: The Lebanese Company for Air Investment (LCAI) has taken full control of Lebanese cargo carrier Trans Mediterranean Airlines under TMA's 60 billion Lebanese pounds ($39 million) capital increase, the airline said on Thursday.
TMA Chairman Fadi Saab said LCAI, majority owned by Beirut banker Farid Raphael, took up all 59,994,000 new shares of 1,000 pounds each issued under the capital increase announced last November.
This raised LCAI's stake in TMA from 73 percent to 99.99 percent, he told Reuters.

"The Lebanese Company for Air Investment has taken up all the increase and paid 25 percent of the amount immediately. The rest will be paid in separate installments on dates to be set later in 1997," Saab said.

Other shareholders like former education minister Najib Abu Haidar who held 10 percent, Druze leader Walid Jumblatt who held six percent and fincancier Georges Yaacoub, five percent, did not take part in the capital increase, he said.
TMA shareholders decided on November 11 to increase the company's capital by cash subscription to 60 billion Lebanese pounds from six million pounds.
The troubled cargo carrier, which has seven aircraft and was profitable before Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war, resumed flights in November after a three-month stoppage for administrative restructuring.
